identity.real_world_identity_notes: The EVO2 is distinct from the earlier Huracan LP 620-2 Super Trofeo. No predecessor telemetry alias is attached to this record.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection in two simulators shows a GT rim closed over the top, without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown. The AMS2 observation first recorded this rim as open-topped, which was wrong: the first Assetto Corsa EVO drive of the same car showed it closed, and re-checking AMS2 confirmed the original reading rather than a difference between the games. No override is written because there is no deviation - both model the same rim.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car moved from rest without physical clutch input. The underlying simulator mechanism was not established.
All six paddle-selected forward gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts without driver lift, with automatic cut perceptible.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with no driver throttle input, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.

The rim's top was corrected from open to closed. A second simulator is what found it: `gt-formula` implies nothing about the top, so an open-top value contradicted no rule and validated cleanly, and no amount of checking this record against itself would have surfaced it. It took another game modelling the same car.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Clutch-free move-off, six no-lift paddle upshifts with automatic cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and the open-top no-display rim were directly observed.
The mechanism permitting clutch-free move-off was not determined.

confidence.basis: The exact identity and complete user-facing control technique were directly checked in AMS2; official sources independently establish the car identity and transmission hardware.

notes: Observed live in AC-EVO 0.8.1 via guided verification observation ac-evo.lamborghini-huracan-st-evo2.20260821t040031522z-061b4845 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Controls directly observed in a guided Assetto Corsa EVO drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and they agree with the AMS2 drive already curated for this car on every field both established.

notes: Observed live in ACC 21257365 via guided verification observation acc.lamborghini-hurac-n-st-evo2-2021.20260822t220556604z-e7a9334c by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: KUNOS's official ACC Challengers Pack page names the Lamborghini Huracan ST EVO2 and the 2021 specification. The live ACC display name, stable internal id and ST class agree with that official identity, while the guided drive directly established the simulator behavior.

claims.basis: Official release and manufacturer material agree with the exact live model and class identity observed through SimHub 9.11.22.
Manufacturer documentation and direct exercise of all six paddle-selected forward gears agree.

Direct testing established clutch-free move-off, clutch-free no-lift upshifts with perceptible cut, and clutch-free downshifts with a visible automatic-blip spike. The move-off mechanism remains explicitly unknown.

Direct cockpit inspection classified a closed-top, no-display rim as GT-style in the project vocabulary. The top was corrected after a second simulator's drive of the same car disagreed and a re-check of AMS2 showed the first reading was the error. Falsified by a cockpit view, in either game, showing rim material absent over the top.
Manufacturer brochure for the EVO2 plus the exact telemetry identity Assetto Corsa EVO reports, which differs in wording from the AMS2 name for the same car and is recorded as its own identity.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

The official ACC DLC page names the 2021 Lamborghini Huracan ST EVO2. SimHub simultaneously reported telemetry name `Lamborghini Huracán ST Evo2 2021`, internal id `lamborghini_huracan_st_evo2`, and class `ST`, so this is the same Super Trofeo EVO2 already curated from Lamborghini, AMS2 and AC EVO evidence rather than the GT3 EVO2 or the earlier LP 620-2 Super Trofeo.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

notes: The old LamborghiniHuracanLP6202SuperTrofeo identity belongs to a different predecessor and is intentionally not included.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Paddle sequential that asks for no clutch at any point: it gets away from rest, cuts the upshift and blips the downshift itself. Once you are in the car the gearbox is not your problem.
